questions.prompt: Which function determines what an authenticated user may do?
questions.explanation: Authorization governs permitted actions.

questions.prompt: Which combination represents distinct authentication-factor categories?

choices.text: A password and a second memorized phrase only.
A password and a possession-based security token.

questions.explanation: Knowledge and possession are separate factor categories.

questions.prompt: What does least privilege mean?

choices.text: Use one shared account for all staff.
Grant only the access needed for authorized responsibilities.

questions.explanation: Least privilege limits unnecessary permissions.

questions.prompt: Why are shared privileged accounts a concern?

choices.text: They weaken individual accountability and access control.

questions.explanation: Shared credentials make actions harder to attribute and govern.

questions.prompt: An employee changes roles but retains incompatible old privileges. What should occur?

choices.text: Reevaluate and remove unnecessary or conflicting access.
Assume a new job title changes system permissions automatically.

questions.explanation: Mover controls must update actual entitlements.

questions.prompt: A quarterly review excludes administrator accounts. What is the control concern?

choices.text: The reviewed access population is incomplete.
The review is complete because most users were included.

questions.explanation: Privileged accounts are important to a complete access review.

questions.prompt: Evaluate four findings from a user-access review. User listing: A terminated user remains active. A transferred employee retains vendor creation and payment approval. All administrators share one account. The review listing excludes service accounts. Objective: Access should be authorized, appropriate to current duties, attributable, and periodically reviewed using a complete population. Required: Control needed for the terminated user.
questions.explanation: Leaver controls should remove unnecessary access promptly.

questions.prompt: Evaluate four findings from a user-access review. User listing: A terminated user remains active. A transferred employee retains vendor creation and payment approval. All administrators share one account. The review listing excludes service accounts. Objective: Access should be authorized, appropriate to current duties, attributable, and periodically reviewed using a complete population. Required: Concern with the transferred employee.
questions.explanation: Role changes must address actual combined entitlements.

questions.prompt: Evaluate four findings from a user-access review. User listing: A terminated user remains active. A transferred employee retains vendor creation and payment approval. All administrators share one account. The review listing excludes service accounts. Objective: Access should be authorized, appropriate to current duties, attributable, and periodically reviewed using a complete population. Required: Concern with the shared administrator account.
questions.explanation: Shared credentials obscure who performed an action.

questions.prompt: Evaluate four findings from a user-access review. User listing: A terminated user remains active. A transferred employee retains vendor creation and payment approval. All administrators share one account. The review listing excludes service accounts. Objective: Access should be authorized, appropriate to current duties, attributable, and periodically reviewed using a complete population. Required: Concern with omitted service accounts.
questions.explanation: Relevant service identities also require governance.

questions.prompt: What is a vulnerability?

choices.text: A weakness that could be exploited or contribute to an adverse event.

questions.explanation: A vulnerability is a weakness, not necessarily an incident or realized loss.

questions.prompt: Which is primarily a detective control?
questions.explanation: Detection identifies potentially adverse events for investigation.

questions.prompt: Which activity belongs in incident response?

choices.text: Containment and analysis while preserving relevant evidence.
Restoring every system without checking the cause.

questions.explanation: Response combines analysis, containment, recovery, and evidence considerations.

questions.prompt: What is a key purpose of lessons learned after an incident?

choices.text: Prove every future incident is impossible.

questions.explanation: Post-incident review turns findings into improvements.

questions.prompt: A critical internet-facing vulnerability and a low-impact isolated finding are discovered. What should guide priority?

choices.text: Only the alphabetical order of system names.
Risk, exposure, impact, and relevant remediation factors.
Always fix the easiest issue first regardless of risk.

questions.explanation: Risk-based prioritization considers the actual exposure and consequences.

questions.prompt: A system produces extensive logs but no one reviews or investigates alerts. What is the concern?

choices.text: Logging volume alone proves control effectiveness.
No monitoring is needed if logs exist.
Detection and escalation may be ineffective despite data collection.

questions.explanation: Collection alone is not a complete detective control.

questions.prompt: Select appropriate actions during a suspected security incident. Observed event: A monitoring alert shows unusual privileged access to confidential records. The team has not confirmed the scope. A technician proposes deleting logs and immediately rebuilding every affected system. Response objectives: Protect the business, preserve useful evidence, determine scope, contain the event, remediate causes, and recover through the approved process. Required: First response to the alert.

choices.text: Validate and triage while preserving relevant evidence
Assume the alert is always false

questions.explanation: Initial analysis establishes the incident’s nature and supports an appropriate response.

questions.prompt: Select appropriate actions during a suspected security incident. Observed event: A monitoring alert shows unusual privileged access to confidential records. The team has not confirmed the scope. A technician proposes deleting logs and immediately rebuilding every affected system. Response objectives: Protect the business, preserve useful evidence, determine scope, contain the event, remediate causes, and recover through the approved process. Required: Response to proposed log deletion.

choices.text: Preserve relevant evidence under the response plan

questions.explanation: Uncontrolled deletion can impede investigation and legal obligations.

questions.prompt: Select appropriate actions during a suspected security incident. Observed event: A monitoring alert shows unusual privileged access to confidential records. The team has not confirmed the scope. A technician proposes deleting logs and immediately rebuilding every affected system. Response objectives: Protect the business, preserve useful evidence, determine scope, contain the event, remediate causes, and recover through the approved process. Required: Objective of containment.

choices.text: Guarantee no prior data was affected
Limit further harm while coordinating the response

questions.explanation: Containment limits ongoing impact without replacing investigation.

questions.prompt: Select appropriate actions during a suspected security incident. Observed event: A monitoring alert shows unusual privileged access to confidential records. The team has not confirmed the scope. A technician proposes deleting logs and immediately rebuilding every affected system. Response objectives: Protect the business, preserve useful evidence, determine scope, contain the event, remediate causes, and recover through the approved process. Required: Post-recovery action.

choices.text: Review causes and improve controls and procedures

questions.explanation: Lessons learned support sustained improvement.

questions.prompt: Which transformation is designed to be reversible with a key?

choices.text: A checksum label without a process.

questions.explanation: Encryption protects recoverable information using keys.

questions.prompt: Which approach is appropriate for password verification storage?

choices.text: A shared reversible key stored with every password.

questions.explanation: Password hashing is designed for verification without storing recoverable plaintext passwords.

questions.prompt: What is a purpose of data classification?

choices.text: Guarantee no employee can ever misuse data.
Determine handling and protection requirements based on sensitivity.

questions.explanation: Classification guides protection and lifecycle controls.

questions.prompt: Which activity belongs to key management?

choices.text: Controlled key generation, access, rotation, and revocation.

questions.explanation: Keys need lifecycle governance and protection.

questions.prompt: Encrypted confidential data and its decryption key are available to the same unauthorized users. What is the concern?

choices.text: Encryption guarantees protection regardless of key access.
Hashing the file name solves every issue.
Key exposure undermines the intended confidentiality protection.

questions.explanation: Users with the key can recover plaintext.

questions.prompt: A confidential backup reaches the end of its required retention period. What should be evaluated?

choices.text: Authorized secure disposal consistent with policy and obligations.
Permanent retention of every copy without review.

questions.explanation: Retention and secure disposal should cover backups as well as active data.

questions.prompt: Evaluate design weaknesses in a data-export service. Service design: Confidential records are encrypted at rest. All support users can retrieve both ciphertext and keys. Passwords are stored in plaintext. Backup copies are never included in retention reviews. Protection goals: Only authorized users should recover confidential data, credentials should be protected appropriately, and retention/disposal should cover all relevant copies. Required: Main key-management improvement.

choices.text: Restrict and monitor key access separately as appropriate

questions.explanation: Control over key material is essential to encryption effectiveness.

questions.prompt: Evaluate design weaknesses in a data-export service. Service design: Confidential records are encrypted at rest. All support users can retrieve both ciphertext and keys. Passwords are stored in plaintext. Backup copies are never included in retention reviews. Protection goals: Only authorized users should recover confidential data, credentials should be protected appropriately, and retention/disposal should cover all relevant copies. Required: Password-storage improvement.

choices.text: Use a suitable salted password-hashing scheme
Use the username as the password

questions.explanation: Password verification should not require plaintext storage.

questions.prompt: Evaluate design weaknesses in a data-export service. Service design: Confidential records are encrypted at rest. All support users can retrieve both ciphertext and keys. Passwords are stored in plaintext. Backup copies are never included in retention reviews. Protection goals: Only authorized users should recover confidential data, credentials should be protected appropriately, and retention/disposal should cover all relevant copies. Required: Retention improvement.

choices.text: Include backups in authorized retention and disposal controls

questions.explanation: Lifecycle controls need to cover relevant copies and obligations.

questions.prompt: Evaluate design weaknesses in a data-export service. Service design: Confidential records are encrypted at rest. All support users can retrieve both ciphertext and keys. Passwords are stored in plaintext. Backup copies are never included in retention reviews. Protection goals: Only authorized users should recover confidential data, credentials should be protected appropriately, and retention/disposal should cover all relevant copies. Required: Effect of broad plaintext export privileges.

choices.text: Access control still matters even when storage is encrypted
All support users are automatically entitled

questions.explanation: Authorized decryption pathways can expose data if permissions are excessive.

questions.prompt: Which concept focuses on the collection, use, retention, and disclosure of personal information?
questions.explanation: Privacy addresses the personal-information lifecycle and applicable commitments.

questions.prompt: HIPAA scope generally requires evaluating which relationship?

choices.text: Whether any employee once visited a doctor.
Covered-entity or business-associate status and applicable activities.
Whether the company uses a spreadsheet.
Whether a website contains a health word.

questions.explanation: HIPAA has defined scope and does not automatically cover every health-related fact everywhere.

questions.prompt: What is PCI DSS?

choices.text: A universal substitute for every privacy law.
A payment-card data security standard with a defined scope.

questions.explanation: PCI DSS addresses payment-card data security; other obligations can also apply.

questions.prompt: Which privacy principle limits collection to information needed for the stated purpose under applicable requirements?
questions.explanation: Minimization reduces unnecessary personal-data processing.

questions.prompt: A company sends personal data to a processor without defining responsibilities or safeguards. What is appropriate?

choices.text: Evaluate applicable processor obligations and establish suitable terms and controls.
Treat a vendor logo as sufficient evidence.

questions.explanation: Third-party processing requires governance under applicable obligations.

questions.prompt: Why map personal-data flows before assessing privacy controls?

choices.text: To understand collection, uses, recipients, locations, and retention.

questions.explanation: A data map supports scope and control evaluation.

questions.prompt: Identify the appropriate scope and control considerations for a new customer platform. Platform facts: The company collects personal information beyond the stated service need, uses an external processor, stores payment-card data, and assumes HIPAA applies solely because a form has a health-related field. Assessment objective: Determine applicable requirements from actual activities and relationships, and evaluate data handling across its lifecycle. Required: Control concern with unnecessary collection.
questions.explanation: Unnecessary collection may exceed the legitimate purpose and increase risk.

questions.prompt: Identify the appropriate scope and control considerations for a new customer platform. choices.text: PCI automatically replaces all privacy law
Applicable PCI DSS requirements and other obligations

questions.explanation: Card-data security has defined requirements that can coexist with other duties.

questions.prompt: Identify the appropriate scope and control considerations for a new customer platform. choices.text: Evaluate covered-entity, business-associate, and activity facts
Assume any health word establishes scope

questions.explanation: Scope depends on the legal relationships and activities.

questions.prompt: Which function is explicitly part of NIST CSF 2.0?
questions.explanation: Govern is one of the six CSF 2.0 functions.

questions.topic: Security Frameworks, Risk Assessment & Control Evaluation
questions.prompt: What is residual risk?

choices.text: Risk before every control in all cases.
Risk remaining after considering the relevant controls or responses.
Only the number of open tickets.

questions.explanation: Residual risk reflects the effect of risk responses and controls.

questions.topic: Security Frameworks, Risk Assessment & Control Evaluation
questions.prompt: What does operating effectiveness address?

choices.text: Only whether a policy was written.
Only whether a control name sounds suitable.
Whether a control worked as intended over the relevant period.

questions.explanation: Operation requires evidence of actual performance.

questions.topic: Security Frameworks, Risk Assessment & Control Evaluation
questions.prompt: What does design suitability ask?

choices.text: Whether the described control can address its intended objective.
Whether every future incident is impossible.
Whether the policy has a signature alone.

questions.explanation: Design links control activities to objectives and risks.

questions.topic: Security Frameworks, Risk Assessment & Control Evaluation
questions.prompt: An access-review control omits the very privileged accounts it is meant to review. What is the issue?

choices.text: The review is effective because it is monthly.
The control population does not support the objective.
All omitted accounts are automatically low risk.

questions.explanation: Frequency cannot cure a population that misses the relevant risk.

questions.topic: Security Frameworks, Risk Assessment & Control Evaluation
questions.prompt: What should an evaluator do with a control exception?

choices.text: Ignore it if most samples passed.
Investigate its cause, extent, significance, and any relevant compensating controls.

questions.explanation: Exceptions require contextual evaluation rather than automatic dismissal or overgeneralization.

questions.topic: Security Frameworks, Risk Assessment & Control Evaluation
questions.prompt: Evaluate an organization’s security-control claims. Claims: Management maps policies to a framework and calls that proof of effectiveness.
